# Chapter Seven: Father and Daughter

> *"For every child says the name of the lord when young, that name is ‘Mother’."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

The arctic gust tore across the snow-covered landscape as the first flakes of the season came to the territory, bathing buildings with the dry granules of white, winter had come early this year as families burrowed into the warm safety of there houses, fireplaces across the land sent smoke towards the sky, from a distance it looked like pillars of black ascending to escape the earth.

The lone bundled figure sat upon the large chestnut horse wrapped head to toe in a snow-white fur to combat the biting cold, a mahogany hilt from the ancient sword poked out of the gathering of alabaster, the ornate brass and red mahogany the only contrast to the white of both snow and rider.

Corliss rode on along the well-traveled farm road towards the keep blocking her eyes from the snow she followed the line of the mountain up into the sky where even now with the low visibility the outline of the large castle stood out against the horizon. The brown appaloosa trudged through two feet of snow in its path, its labored breathing steaming from his nostrils.

Gently she guided the large animal along what she assumed was the road, navigating simply by the ridges along the edges or the intermittent fence lines of the passing farms, passing one such homestead she watched as two young men went about the morning chores bundled up in fur and leather as they rushed to get there tasks complete both young men making haste to return to the warmth of the main house.

They paused, watching the stranger with open surprise to see anyone traveling the road in weather like this. Corliss nodded at the two boys as she passed the farm, both young men waving back and continuing to watch her long after she had passed the yard.

She spent the time watching the old stone keep growing larger as she approached, passing the properties she came upon the round fence of the small village, eyeing the large airship as it emerged out of the snow, the wooden behemoth standing sentry over the small town, she narrowed her eyes at the unusual sight.

“Galen has company” she said to herself.

Finally, reaching the old gates of the castle, a miserable looking guard waved her in, She continued up the hill for a little ways finally coming to the main courtyard of the tall keep, looking up she could see the worn but solid stone that covered the old castle, it had stood for centuries but still looked strong she thought dismounting by the stables, she threw a filthy young man a silverling, he pocketed the small coin smiling at Corliss showing the last three of his good teeth as he took the reins of her horse leading him gently and expertly into the warm and dry stables.

Reaching the top of the steps the large solid doors opened slowly as a gust of warm air greeted her on the landing. A gaunt man adorned in brightly colored robes ushered her in closing the door behind her.

“I am Warden Corliss here to see Seer Bor” she stated before the man could ask. With a simple nod he quickly guided her into the main chamber.

Entering the large ornate room, she found Galen, her father sitting atop the old throne that was used for official business in the territory. She forced herself not to roll her eyes as she walked forward the pompous prick she thought.

Gritting her teeth Corliss bowed to the man who had abandoned her mother and herself for the glory of power and money. Galen motioned for the warden to rise.

“Why am I here father” Corliss asked her tone devoid of any happiness or familiarity with the old man, Galen winced slightly nodding to the Warden.

He looks old she thought studying her father, his gaunt frame looking fragile as he sat upon the large stone throne, the deep purple of the long robes of his office looked more like they were draped over a corpse instead of a live human.

His white hair unkempt where it stuck out of the tall cap that sat upon his head.

Galen’s steel grey eyes roved over Corliss making her uncomfortable, but she could see desperation in his eyes and to her surprise sadness, as if he were trying to figure out how to connect with her, reach her on a personal level but not able to, for a moment she almost softened, almost felt sorry for him.

Then the memories of what his leaving had done to her and the vision of her mother, wasting away in a filthy bed, calling Galen’s name washing over her mind in vivid detail, her face hardening at the thought.

“Corliss, I have summoned you because I know of no better Warden in the territory and we have a situation that requires your expertise” he began but Corliss held up the leather-gloved hand to stop the old man.

“Flattery will get you nowhere father, just tell me why I am here” she stated coldly, she could see the annoyed look on the old man’s face,

Corliss nearly smiled. Good, let him be the one who feels frustrated for once, she thought.

After a moment Galen nodded, “Things in the kingdom are in flux Warden,” he began, using her title instead of her name, the change did not escape Corliss.

“The emperor has died, and the Empress has dispatched troops to locate something that fell to earth; however, they have been unsuccessful. I also have reports that Lusor and Dever have soldiers that have crossed the border despite the rising tensions with both nations; they are also looking for this thing. Whatever it is, it has countries scrambling to find it, and I need to ensure it doesn’t fall into the wrong hands,” he said pausing on the last word as if searching for and failing to find a better description.

“I am commissioning you with finding it Corliss, when you have, return it here. With everyone out to obtain it, this item or thing poses a safety risk to the land” he stated, and Corliss narrowed her gaze at him.

He was playing an angle and she knew it.

Wardens were subject to the crowns request and Galen being a Lord Seer was able to make such a request, she could accept or turn it over to another Warden, there was no way she could outright refuse him, her father knew it too, he was a master politician, smug bastard she thought and considered passing it up, giving to another Warden, just to see the look on his face.

But what he had said intrigued her, why would Dever and Lusor send troops into Vicor, what were they looking for, what could be so important, that made no sense she thought.

“Fine, I will accept this mission and find out what fell from the sky, give me what information you have she stated and then thought of the soldiers, if others were also seeking this thing, then that introduces another element of danger, I will need to conscript two of your best soldiers, no more I need to move fast and quiet, at least until I get out of the area, then I am better on my own” she stated, Galen contemplated this for a moment and then slowly nodded.

“That is within your right, you will have my two best soldiers, rest assured they are worth an entire battalion” he stated and motioned at the small assistant who bowed and left the room.

“I will leave once the soldiers are ready” she said, and Galen sat forward a twinkle in his eye

“Why don’t you stay for dinner before riding out, I can have the kitchen make up whatever you like daughter,” Galen said, his tone becoming gentle and inviting Corliss knew he was trying but there was too much history between the two to simply forget what had happened.

The picture of her mother once again materialized within her mind, the old anger returning, pouring salt into the wound.

Corliss bit down on the anger, not trusting herself to speak, she simply shook her head. The old Seer’s face fell in disappointment, pain filling his eyes, but nodding in understanding.

Corliss felt a guilt stab of guilt, the old man was trying, trying to mend a relationship that had long ago been broken.

She couldn’t get past the hatred in her heart for his actions, for the death of her mother and for how he had abandoned her, he had been the one who had broken there home, forcing her to grow up far too soon and a string of memories, some that still haunted her late in the night flashed through her thoughts.

Corliss dismissed herself turning her back on her father and walking out of the large room. She would wait for the soldiers, though requesting them annoyed her.

Wardens worked alone, but she swallowed her pride, this was not a simple mission and she would quite probably need backup, she had a right to request the escort, she would use them at least until she felt she was far enough out of the area not to run into a contingent of hostile soldiers.

As she left through the large archway and the doors were closing, she heard her father call.

“Sooner or later daughter, you will need to forgive me” he said. Corliss set her jaw and refused to answer the man.

After exiting the keep, she found her horse and quickly set to provisioning for the trip.

The young man went about his job proficiently, ensuring that Corliss had her list of supplies quickly delivered, which earned him another silverling, his smile at the reward revealing the yellow and decaying teeth of someone in the working class.

She watched as he laid out the items carefully, despite his frayed shirt and dirty hands, the young man had a practiced efficiency in the way he moved and Corliss smiled in appreciation as he loaded her packs, The working class so often went overlooked by those in power she thought, watching him work, but hadn’t that always been the way, people in power under the illusion they were in control, Corliss had a much broader view, knowing that without people like this young man, the Lords and Ladies world would crumble.

“So, we are to escort you then,” came an annoyed voice from behind the Warden shaking her from her reverie. Turning she found a large soldier with a bald head and sour look on his face, next to him was a petite, strikingly beautiful angel with blonde hair but Corliss did not miss the predatory look in her eyes, she was a killer.

Sizing the soldiers up Corliss could see they were not rookies, from the worn weapons and scars visible on their hands and face, these two had seen more than their fair share of combat.

Good, she thought. At least Galen had given her capable people, a small worry nagging at her, she had requested the two soldiers, just enough to move unseen and move fast. They had better be his best she thought.

The small group would be outnumbered, for a moment she doubted her decision, should she opt for a larger contingent she wondered, her stomach twisted at the thought of going back to her father for more and dismissed the idea, she would make it work.

“Yes, I am are the two of you ready to ride?” she said and they nodded, the female soldier came over and stood in front of Corliss “Lord Galen is sending his best with you, we are worth two entire squads of soldiers and we can move light and quick, do not fret Warden, you are in good hands” she finished as If reading the Warden’s thoughts and Corliss met her eyes and could see the determination if anything this woman believed she was telling the truth so Corliss nodded to her, she would have to trust the soldiers assessment, for now.

A flurry of bright cloth caught Corliss’s attention as it passed outside the door, moving to look around the soldier as she caught sight of the small assistant who had been with her father in the main chamber, he looked practically flustered as the small man came running over carrying a stack of parchment

“Warden, your father asked me to give you this, it’s everything we have on the event and what might have fallen to earth” he stated handing the packet to Corliss. She spied the little man and could see the discomfort at being around the horses and smiled.

He was not one for manual labor she thought as she thanked him and quickly reviewed the notes, frowning at just how little was there, after a moment she nodded to the soldiers.

“It looks like we are heading east, so mount up” she ordered.

“So…the Empress goes nuts over finding some piece of rock that fell from the sky, old Galen catches wind of it and decides whatever it is, he better find it first and earn some ass kissing points, I mean Mephis’s balls what could have possible come down from the sky that is so fucking important he sends two of his elite guard and a damn Warden to find it”.

The one named Borik said loudly as if speaking to an large audience instead of the trio as they rode down through a shaded path the morning sun playing with shadows through the few leaves left upon the trees.

Shaking his head, his female compatriot shook her head a wry smile spreading across her face “Shut up Borik, you are never happy unless you are complaining” she shot at him, the big man crossed his arms over his chest and sulked but did so quietly.

Corliss had come to find out her name was Starish, the other woman had the look of a marksman, her eyes never wavering in ensuring they were assessing the tree line for threats, she was, aside from Corliss the groups most accomplished tracker and sniper if the loud brash Borik was to believed,

Borik might be brash but when speaking to Starish there was nothing but respect for the woman, the rifle she carried was so long, half of it would stick over her shoulder when strapped to her back, there wasn’t a person alive Borik had intimated to Corliss that could hit a target with more accuracy then Starish.

“You were sent because I needed backup, if there are indeed enemy soldiers in the area then your being here will be to my advantage, so Borik, stop complaining” Corliss said from her position at the front of the small group.

After a few minutes Corliss did turn to the small group “I noticed the airship in town, who came to see Galen?” she asked curiously and caught the wince from Borik “Some trumped up asshat from the capital, here to fill the Lord Seer in on the changes since the Emperor’s death” he simply said, Corliss turned to him and with an astonished look whispered “The Emperor’s dead?” and Borik blanched a little.

“Um, yeah it just happened, or at least we are just hearing about it, I’m sorry, I thought Galen would have told you” he finished the annoyance in his tone was gone, Corliss had a million questions, but kept them to herself for now, thinking back to the Keep, the preparations and the worried look on Uri’s face, he had known, damn him he had and didn’t tell her a thing she thought as anger shot through her.

She rode silently with her thoughts as her chestnut mare led the way through the now light flakes of snow that descended through the trees just starting to cover the ground as a frigid northerly wind assaulted the group forcing them to tighten their hold on the heavy coats that adorned their uniformed bodies.

Corliss had reviewed the notes Galen had given her, they were vague at best she thought, but enough to point her in the general location, no one actually knew what had fallen.

Only that everyone seemed to be looking for it she mused.

Whatever this thing was it had Galen scrambling to find it before anyone else she thought with a slight smile.

“So, what do we know about this thing, is it a bird or an angel or Aurtus himself come to earth” Borik asked his baritone voice loud enough that the entire small precession heard it.

Corliss shook her head “You know what we know Borik, now quiet before I give you scout duty” she threatened and knew that would keep the man quiet for about two minutes.

Borik was overweight, loud, obnoxious and a drunkard she suspected from the way he looked at her he was a womanizer as well, Starish came to ride next to Corliss silently regarding the other woman.

After a few moments Corliss broke the silence “So, after spending very little time with both of you, I have to ask, why does Galen keep that guy around?” she asked in a hushed town, motioning her head back towards the belching and complaining Borik bringing up the rear.

Starish looked back and smiled, shaking her head “Because though his is a lot of things and none of them good, when he is on duty, the man is a force of nature, I once watched as he took out an entire contingent of troops with those two hammers and that cannon, never stopping and never tiring, despite being shot several times during the fight” she began and the smile disappeared and she leveled a serious look at Corliss “There is no better soldier to have at your side Warden” she finished and Corliss nodded.

Looking back Corliss eyed the large metal tube and engraved wooden stock strapped to Borik’s saddle, she had never seen it’s like and spent a few moments admiring its construction. The cannon was something new it had only been in service for the last year or so but in that time, it had proven worth its weight in crystal.

Borik was the only person on the team who was large enough to handle the beast of a weapon, it fired a resin ball five times the size of the ones they used for the rifles and pistols, the energy spreading out in a cone it wasn’t good for distance but close up, there wasn’t a more lethal weapon.

Studying the weapon, she could see the high polish along the worn bluing of the barrel and the freshly waxed stock, Borik doted on the damn gun she mused.

The large man rubbed his bald head which despite the cold had a wet sheen of perspiration, that coupled with the distillery smell coming from his general direction told Corliss the man was hungover if not still drunk, moving forward a bit she tried to distance herself from the distillery smell.

Starish joined her, quietly bringing her white stallion to walk next to Corliss, the soldier was the complete opposite to Borik where he was brash, she was subtle and where he was loud the woman was completely silent.

Starish rode next to the Warden for a good ten minutes before uttering a word.

“Do we really not know more than the general direction, I don’t mind telling you Warden, I don’t like riding into this kind of situation when we don’t even know if it’s dangerous or not” she whispered turning to look at her and regarding Corliss with those emerald green eyes that tended to get her proposed to in every bar this side of the territories.

Corliss organized her thoughts. Taking the time to pat the large chestnut beast, Starish was right and it was bothering The Warden to no end. She was sure her father did not want her dead, though had it been anyone else, the entire mission would smell of a trap.

Riding into a situation with little or no information was not uncommon, but this was also not your typical retrieval she thought. Corliss brandished the small stack of parchment and waved it in front of Starish.

“This is all the information they have, though from these reports he gave us I would assume danger. I don’t think a contingent of troops from Lusor or Dever would have any issue killing the likes of us” she said as Starish gently took the stack and began to carefully go through it.

Something about the entire thing bothered Corliss, why hadn’t Galen handed her a missive from the Empress she wondered then her jaw setting firmly answering her own question, you know why, because he wants to find it before she does so he can use it in his stupid power games and now you're mixed up in them too. Congratulations you are your fathers pawn Corliss chided herself.

The group rode for most of the day, the winter landscape cold but breathtakingly beautiful giving the world an almost surreal feeling as they continued east along the old trade routes and farm trails, finally as the sun began to descend behind the line of trees the group set up camp.

Starish sat on watch while Corliss warmed herself by the fire looking out towards the tree the other woman used as a firing blind, the location giving her a good view of the area and making it nearly impossible for her to be spotted.

“She always does that. She will sleep like that all night. It’s not that she is scared, mind you, she just likes the height.” Borik said from across the fire also looking out towards Starish.

“That woman is the hammer of Aurtus with that gun, should we find ourselves in the thick of it, you will be glad she is here,” he finished and Corliss could see the complete belief in his statement, This rough soldier trusted that woman with his life and that was no small thing.

Corliss found a tree that enough leaves left on the branches that the snow hadn’t permeated to the ground, Settling in with her back against a tree, she closed her eyes listening to the sounds of the forest around her, she caught a light whistle in the air and looked up to see Starish pointing above her, looking up Corliss could make out the glow of the small monkeys as they shot from branch to branch and smiled.

They stayed clear of the ground, probably from the loud grunting noised from Borik as he sat across from the fire noisily eating a piece of the rabbit Starish had caught and left for them.

At least he is sober now she thought to herself trying to suppress the smile that wanted to spread across her face.

“So, what’s the plan from here Warden? I assume we are not just going for a leisurely ride until we run into something that doesn’t look like it’s from around here,” Borik called over, the half-eaten piece of rabbit showing itself in his mouth as he spoke.

Corliss made a disgusted noise and shook her head. “Please finish your food before you talk,” Borik gave her a sheepish grin and a shrug though he did swallow, opening his mouth to show her, his grin turning wicked as the Warden rolled her eyes at the childish behavior.

Corliss regarded the fire. Honestly, she didn’t know what the hell they were going to do, but she wasn’t going to tell Borik that. Corliss had thought about questioning the villagers they came across but unless they were incredibly lucky, they weren’t likely to get far with that, they had a general direction and an approximation of distance, that was all.

There was only one place she could think to go where they would find information, the only place where she knew they would have seen the thing fall and would be able to point them at its destination.

“We are going to ask the seven sisters” she said the other man stopping mid-chew and looking at her as a flash of fear passed over his face, the look was almost comical, and Corliss had to suppress a laugh.

“No, not them! Please tell me we are not going to that damn convent. I hate that place, and they hate me,” Borik pleaded, causing Corliss to cover her mouth with a fake cough to hide the smile.

“Oh, they love you” Starish said causing the large man to jump “Mephis’s ass, you need to stop sneaking up on people woman” he barked. Starish curled up by the fire and motioned to the big man.

“Dinner for me, watch for you” she said and with a grumble Borik rose, picking up the large hand cannon and skulking into the woods. Turning to Corliss she motioned back towards the woods where they both could hear Borik still grumbling “We were on a patrol about a year ago, The captain had a relationship with the seven sisters and we ended up there to resupply, so Borik is hanging out with the nun’s and tries to proposition one, she doesn’t understand what he is talking about so he shows her his wares” Starish began. Leaning in Corliss laughed at this last part.

“The mother superior comes out to find one of her nuns passed out on the ground and Borik with his pants around his ankles, oh that woman kicked his ass up one side and down the other before banishing him from the convent, he had to spend two days outside in the rain while we rested before the trip back”. She finished picking up a piece of rabbit and beginning to eat while Corliss just sat there chuckling.

“Despite Borik’s reservations, if anyone has seen anything it would be them from there vantage point on top of the mountain that overlooks the entire area” Corliss began, then raising her voice she yelled after the big man.

“Borik, if it makes you feel better I will leave you out on sentry while Starish and I go in” Only a loud grumble returned the statement and both women laughed “it’s possible the Mother superior has passed on, she was pretty old the last time I saw her and that was nearly two years ago” she said to Starish Borik poked his head out of the brush and upon seeing the Warden smiling at him shot her an evil look and shook his head.

“There is no way she is dead, that woman would outlive every one of us on sheer evil alone” he spat returning to watch as Starish ate.

A few days later the trio rode up to the gates of the ancient fortress that housed the seven sisters and their order.

As she had promised, Corliss had left Borik on patrol ensuring he wouldn’t have to see the old woman but that was more for her benefit then Borik’s bringing him in the convent if the old mother superior were still alive would probably get them all thrown out she thought still smiling over Borik’s tale.

Corliss felt it best not to start off a conversation with Borik there to remind the sisters how horrible soldiers can be.

She stepped off her horse and walked the few paces to the large wooden gate. Pounding on it, she waited a few moments before finally hearing an elderly voice call from the ramparts above. “Who goes there?” the reedy voice called, and Corliss looked up to see the face of the order’s mother superior as she peered suspiciously over the edge of the wall.

Her full white habit held down as the wind tried to carry it away. “It is Warden Corliss Mother Superior, I have been here before, with Uri, I come to ask for information” she stated loudly so the old woman could hear her. After a moment the woman nodded, giving Corliss a severe look.

“How is the old bear, still alive?” she called down and Corliss tried to hide the smile “Yes Mother Superior, he sends his best”.

The old woman shook her head and disappeared over the large wall.

“I am old Warden; not deaf you may keep your voice down” she huffed and out of the corner of her eye she could see Starish stifle a grin at the comment.

Corliss simply shot her an annoyed look but that didn’t seem to dissuade the sniper, in fact it only made her grin larger. Shaking her head and continuing her annoyed look at Starish they waited for a moment until she heard the loud thud of the big wooden bolt being withdrawn, and the gate began to open.

Corliss could see the look on Starish’s face as she peeked into the courtyard, the same look she had given when first entering this place as a junior warden the first time Uri had introduced her to the order. The well-groomed garden, covered in snow, full of statues of saints and in the center, a large man on a wooden cross stood as the centerpiece.

She stifled a smile as Starish’s eyes moved from the courtyard and up, scanning the old stone ramparts, it seemed everyone thought this place to easy to attack, until they saw… she thought and watched Starish closely knowing exactly when she found them.

Her eyes went wide, and she whistled as the four large ballistae were wheeled on tracks back into the various guard posts, the castle looked old and falling apart, covered over with vines and ivy It was easy to miss the newly repaired stone and brick that the plants hid and the ancient wooden weapons, that despite their age were well maintained and ready to deliver death on unwelcome guests.

Anyone coming in here, would have a very bad day Corliss thought. For a moment Starish looked curiously at the large wooden cross in the center of the courtyard her eyes going over the thorn crown on his head and the wounds on his side.

“Is that Aurtus?” she asked worried. From her perspective it looked as if they had killed her god. Corliss smiled and shook her head “No, it’s the son of their god, he was killed, and they revere both he and his father” she finished recalling her having a similar conversation when Uri explained it to her, long ago when she had been a young teen and Uri still her mentor, Starish shook her head confused.

“Some of these ancient religions are dark Warden” she whispered still staring at the cross. They moved their horses into the courtyard, looking around Corliss could see the gardens beautiful but devoid of life and covered with snow, in the summer the plants and colors that inhabited them would be breathtaking, but now, like the rest of the land everything was cold, white and dead until the first thaw of spring arrived.

Two of the younger sisters appeared from the large brick chapel that stood center in the courtyard. Taking the reins of the horses as the two dismounted, the sisters gently urged the beasts along with them to the stables, their white dresses and habits blending in with the snow.

“Do not worry Warden, the sisters will ensure your horses are fed and stay warm for the duration of your short visit” Mother superior stated.

She accentuated the word short at the same time giving Corliss an annoyed look. The Warden knew the sisters did not like visitors, it disrupted their schedule and gave the younger sisters ideas best not encouraged when they met women who worked positions the mother thought best suited for men in what the Mother Superior thought was a vain attempt to show men they were there equal.

Corliss recalled the Mother Superior saying something to that effect the last time she had visited and bristled at the memory, the woman could be misogynistic at the best of times.

The Mother superior motioned for the two women to join her as she entered the chapel, once inside she guided them to the left, it was set up similar to the keep’s the messengers preached in, all the way down to the private quarters off of the main worship area Corliss thought.

Starish surveyed the grand room, obviously impressed. Once they had made their way through the cavernous main chamber and into the small quarters the Mother Superior kept as her office, its only furniture a table and three chairs.

The old woman removed the full habit revealing a large mass of long white hair that fell full way down her back as she shook it out, loosening the kinks in a long-practiced action as she walked around the table with a sigh of relief slumping into the chair and motioning to the two to take the seats opposite her.

“So, Warden, I would say it’s good to see you, but we both know I would be lying, so what can I do for you this time” she stated her dislike of Corliss worn like a badge of honor across her statement.

Starish looked from her to the warden she could tell there was a story there, but now was probably not the time to ask, so she remained quiet, finding an interesting knot on the table to stare at instead.

Corliss smiled her sweetest smile and she could see by the look the Mother gave her that it wasn’t working, nor would it get her any traction in this situation.

So, with a sigh, she took the direct approach. “Something came down from the sky at least one-month past, maybe two, we are looking for it. Since your view from the mountain gives you an excellent vantage point for anything that goes on for miles in the eastern territory, I thought you might have seen something” she said and waited for the woman to answer. She surprised them both with a smile and a nod.

“Yes, you are talking about the metal tear on the cloud of fire,” she said. Corliss had no idea what the woman was talking about but nodded anyway, she felt a rush of excitement, that was just odd enough to be what the entire territories seemed to be scouring the world for.

The Mother Superior rose from her seat and walked over to the large rectangular window, opening it she motioned, and Corliss came over to stand next to the old woman, seeing that the window gave an excellent view of the entire western region for miles.

She pointed towards two hills and then moved her hand slightly to the left of them. “It came down about there, six or seven miles out, I don’t have any better information for you, but I will tell you, you cannot miss it, it was like nothing you have ever seen Warden” she finished and Corliss studied the area from the window, burning to memory the area and any landmarks that might help her narrow down there search.

“Thank you, Mother Superior, we will get out of your hair now” she said and from her bag pulled a small handful of Silverling coins and handed them to the woman.

Mother Superior took them and bowed her head in thanks. With a motion to Starish Corliss began to head towards the door when Mother Superior’s words stopped her short.

“You are not the first to look for its Warden, be careful for at least two other groups were seen and of the two, one of them did not look very friendly” she said by way of a warning and Corliss locked eyes with her.

She could see the worry, whoever had come had scared these women and the Warden silently vowed that if she found them, she would spend some quality time making them regret scaring these women of faith she thought she might not agree with the Mother Superior, but she had taken in and helped a lot of broken women over the decades, Corliss had a lot of respect for her mission.

But to the mother superior she only nodded, leaving the room and gently closing the door. They left the fort, they made their way down the mountain, carefully negotiating the trails until they reached Borik as he sat atop his horse, keeping an eye out on the trails below.

“Mother Superior said hello, Borik, and that she missed you,” Corliss said as they made it to their friend.

Borik cocked his head and looked surprised. “Really?” he asked and she could hear the hope in his voice, this more than his innocent look caused the warden to laugh heartily.

“No, Borik, not even close” she shot at him and with an angry curse-filled grumble he turned the horse joining the group as they continued down the hill.

Starish turned to regard the Warden a lock of blonde hair that usually stayed wrapped tight in a bun under the large dirty sun hat played over her cheek “Who were those women?” she asked leaning in towards Corliss.

Looking out over the white landscape unfolding out below her, she pulled the large fur jacket closer to her body as a gust of wind threatened to chill her to the bone.

“They are an old religion, one that worships a god that killed his son and something about a cross, that statue in the courtyard sums it up” she said turning to regard the sniper.

Starish cocked her head and squinting her sea-blue eyes at the Warden worked through what she was saying. “That’s twisted” she answered, and Corliss smiled.

“You should see them on worship days, they eat the body and blood of the son” she said making a clicking sound and moving the horse forward down the steep mountain path.

Leaving the young woman wide-eyed and looking back at the shadow of the keep looming on top of the small mountain

“Aurtus preserve us, really damn dark,” she whispered staring at the looming silhouette of the castle and after a moment of regarding the structure with wide questioning eyes, she turned her horse and urged him into a trot to catch up with the group.

They carefully made their way down the trail with Corliss in the lead smiling as she listened to the two soldiers’ comment on the old religion the sisters practiced. “I don’t think they actually eat body parts and drink cups of blood. I mean have you seen those women,” Borik said, shaking his head as Sharisa shared the warden’s words with the other man.

Corliss could hear the nervous tone in the woman’s voice as she spoke “I don’t know, I have seen some pretty weird stuff with some of these ancient pagan religions, I mean remember those guys who used to cut on the cocks of kids?” she said, shivering at the thought of it.

Corliss rolled her eyes. “It was a circumcision. They weren’t cutting on the kids. It’s a medical thing,” she yelled back, admonishing her for the description.

“Come on, guys, there are a lot of old religions, some dating all the way back to the ancients that people still practice. It’s not our place to judge them as long as it brings no harm.

Remember the words of the emissary,” she said, recalling the doctrines those who practice WIC live by, one of the tenants being understand and embrace those who are different from you.

“You’re right. I should learn to practice the tenants more,” she answered sheepishly. Starish wasn’t overly religious but she did attend assembly once a week from what Borik had intimated.

The group descended into the snow-covered western valley in search of a metal tear as the Mother superior called it. The day waned on, as the trio continued west, Corliss doing her best to resolve the aerial view of the area with their current location.

Dusk had finally begun to settle when Starish rapidly made her way back to the group after riding ahead to scout the trail, coming to ride along next to the Warden, Corliss noticing her body language, the woman was on edge.

“Lady didn’t the Mother mention we weren’t the only ones out here looking?” she questioned, and Corliss turned regarding her for a moment watching as her eyes darted towards the forests edge, and her mouth was set into a perpetual frown.

The warden shook her head running her hand through her long blonde hair, a nervous habit she had picked up as a teen “What are you seeing” she asked, if Starish noticed something and it was bothering her this much then it must be bad she thought bracing herself for the bad news.

Starish stared closely, her eyes roving over every contour of the worn trade path. Finally, she spoke.

“Multiple horse tracks and from the look of the depth, they were weighed down by more than just people, possibly full sets of supplies, looking at these shoe prints, these weren’t merchant’s sir, these were soldiers’ boots. I guess about ten of them came out this way, some walking, others on horseback, just about a half-day ahead of us. “she finished, waiting to hear the warden’s orders.

The sisters had warned they were not the first to come out here looking and from the way she had said it, at least one group was dangerous. Corliss looked around studying the terrain, they were alone so whoever it was, was in front of them and that meant they very possibly would find the prize before they could, Corliss was a warden, failure was not an option for her.

She went through options finally settling on the only course that allowed them any margin of success. “Break out the night lights” she finally said stopping the group and climbing down from the sturdy chestnut animal. The two soldiers followed suit, both climbing down and rustling through the saddlebags carried on the rear of their horses. Corliss pulled out a small wooden box with a leather harness and walking around to the front of the horse, she began to attach it to the underside of the beast’s neck buckling it onto the bridle and harness. The box was small in size only about six inches. Looking back, she could see the soldiers doing the same. Once they were done the small box hung comfortably under the horse’s neck. Corliss turned the small turn screw and watched as the two crystals inside came together lighting up the inside of the box. A shroud over the opening that faced outward kept the light pointed downward and also ensured that it was not easily visible to anyone nearby.

With the horse lamp in place the three mounted and rode on, the small amount of light shining at the ground in front of the horses allowing them to move slowly along and giving them the ability to see the terrain directly in front of them.

Corliss listened and smiled they were professional soldiers; every buckle and tie had been secured to ensure that no noise was created as the horses moved forward down the path. They continued along the trail for almost two hours before Starish, who had ridden ahead again came slinking back to the group, pointing into the distance Corliss could see trace ambient light as it played over the dark trees from a fire in the distance.

“I found their camp,” she whispered and with a motion of her hand Borik carefully climbed down from his horse checking the pistols that rested under his gut and set snugly onto his belt he pulled the large resin cannon and threw the strap over his arm, the cannon hung under his arm within easy reach should he need it.

He then pulled the two war hammers from there place on the saddle and threw them over his back onto the harness that held them, with an easy twist they would come loose in his hand, a gift from a leatherworker in the village for helping him gather skins.

“What’s the plan Lady?” he whispered coming over to stand with Starish who was checking the large brass tube that sat atop the very long rifle, it held two clear crystals that when matched would allow her to see great distances, the only issue was it was sensitive and always required adjusting.

She had marked both crystals allowing her to align the marks without needing to retarget the weapon by firing it, once she was done the sniper gently placed the weapon on her back, joining Borik, they both knelt down next to Corliss.

They tried in vain to get a better look at the location of the camp, but the dense trees and brush prevented them from seeing their competition.

Corliss glanced at the two soldiers, with a motion of her left hand they nodded and moved out, spreading over the area and dividing, the three merging into the Woodline like ghosts, vanishing into the trees.

Carefully they negotiated the underbrush, gently moving branches to ensure they didn’t break or snap back against a tree causing undue noise. Corliss moving away to the right making her way over the wintry surface of the woods getting closer to the bright fire that lit the area. As she moved in, she could hear laughter and conversation echoing through the trees, the soldiers were at ease, no sound discipline she thought, that would make things easier.

Coming around a large trunk she got her first good look at the camp. Counting the bodies, she could see twenty soldiers and cursed quietly.

They were experienced soldiers, not just young men in uniform she realized the bearing and the way they moved and held themselves gave it away, there clothing was civilian, the entire group wore clothes that made them look like traveling merchants. It was the bearing you couldn’t hide easily.

They carried no banners and held no shields with Sigils on them, the weapons they carried were generic and unmarked, these were black soldiers sent to complete a mission where if they were caught no one would come to claim them.

Corliss didn’t expect a blackguard contingent; these complicated matters greatly she thought cursing under her breath. A blackguard would also mean they didn’t want witnesses, if she or the soldiers were caught then they would be executed and left out here in the woods.

Looking to her left she caught sight of Borik, Corliss pointed to the soldiers and waited it took only a minute for him to survey the group and as The Warden watched his eyes went wide and he nodded solemnly to her.

The stakes just went up and with twenty against three the odds were not in their favor. This couldn’t be a straight-up fight and Corliss knew it, first she had to know if these men would fight to the death, she was not one to kill easily.

Cupping her hands an eerie sound emitted from them like that of a lonely night owl, she repeated it three times and then retreated to the horses. After a few moments the other two appeared as well.

Corliss gathered them around. “They severely outnumber us, and we don’t know their intentions, so we wait until they go to sleep, grab a lookout and find out what we can, from there we will make our plan” she said and the soldiers nodded in unison.

Corliss crouched in the brush, keeping her breathing calm as one of the merchants walked the perimeter, oblivious to the impending danger, as he passed Corliss rose quietly, covering the man’s mouth with her hand, she kicked the back of the knee at the same time. From his perspective, she knew it would be shocking and disorienting, one moment he was walking along looking out over the wooded scenery and the next.

He lay on his back with a cold blade pressed against the artery on his neck.

Corliss stared into the terrified eyes of the young man, his bearing might say soldier, but he had pulled night duty, making him the rookie Corliss thought.

“I am going to uncover your mouth, your first reaction will be to call out for help, know this if you do, I will simply drive this blade into your neck and you will die quickly, your friends might come and find us, they might not, but either way you will be dead, do you understand” the Warden whispered.

The guard only took a moment to decide and slowly nodded his head. The hand came off of his mouth and the soldier took a steadying breath, looking up into cold green eyes framed by a mane of blonde hair.

Shaking his head the guard couldn’t take his eyes off of Corliss,, “never in my life have I ever seen anything so beautiful and so deadly at the same time” the young man whispered. Corliss smiled down at the man, but as the smile disappeared the look that replaced it could have turned the blood of a sociopath cold.

Corliss sat there for thirty minutes questioning the man, learning everything she needed to, these were indeed a blackguard though the soldier would not tell her who they worked for.

Corliss guessed the man’s family was threatened should it get out who they worked for, then the families would pay the price.

This group had been ordered to kill anyone they came across without hesitation.

They had been tasked with retrieving the fallen object, but he wouldn’t say where they were to bring it. The young soldier didn’t know much about it but according to him their captain knew a great deal including how big and how much it would weigh which is why they had brought the large ropes and extra horses.

Once Corliss thought she had gotten everything he could out of the man, she thanked him and then covering his mouth and nose, held the struggling man down until he passed out.

Checking his breathing and heart rate she sighed, the man would live, he would have a hell of a headache when he woke, but that was one less face to torment her in the night, the time between waking and sleep where the men she had killed came to visit her, to torment her, the older she got the more crowded that time became. Corliss thought, retreating back to the rendezvous point.

Once she made it back, the three gathered once more “The team is like we thought, black guard, they are here for the same thing, they seem to have better intel but I don’t know who they are working for, the only good news in that is, if this team disappears then whoever sent them won’t come looking for them.

It’s going to be a stealth run “she finished and the other two nodded “Like Verlenshade” Starish said and Corliss studied the sniper, the look in her eyes was haunted as she remembered the mission, Corliss had memories of missions like that, the ones that awoke you in the wee hours of the morning screaming, she nodded to the sniper, both women locking eyes in understanding.

“Let’s hope not,” Corliss simply said, if the look in Starish’s eyes was any clue, that was not a mission they wanted a repeat of. The three slowly moved through the woods entering the outskirts of the camp as the soldiers slept scattered around the fire and in the tents.

Corliss came at the camp putting the small line of tents between herself and the fire ensuring no shadows would play across the fabric giving away her position.

She knew Borik was on the other side doing the same thing leaving Starish on overwatch. She would have found a tree or high ground and with her gun, what had Borik said, she was the fist of Aurtus, no one escaped her notice, nor her aim.

Corliss approached the first tent, listening she could hear the controlled breathing from inside. Hunching down by the cloth, slowly she pulled the knife from her belt, calming her breathing. Lifting the cloth gently, she paused, listening for any change in the man’s breathing, once she was satisfied there was none, she finished pulling back the cloth to reveal the head of the man lying there, fast asleep, before she could think about it Corliss quickly held down the man’s head thrusting the knife into the base of his skull holding it there for a moment, listening for any sounds of alarm from the camp.

Nothing but dead silence as she rose letting go of the dead man’s head and removing the knife, wiping the blade on the side of the tent, as she moved to the next one.

The smell of bodily waste rose from behind her as the man’s bowels let go at the moment of his demise. Corliss did her best to ignore it, continuing to the next tent in the row.

Repeating the kill she went from tent to tent-like an angel of death returning the soldiers to their maker, looking across the way, she could just barely make out Borik mimicking her.

As Corliss made it to the last tent, she continued to add more faces to that crowd of the dead that lived in her mind, their faces seared forever into her consciousness.

She steadied her hand as adrenaline coursed through her system. Beginning to reach for the tent cloth a blue trail of energy shot past her shoulder, close enough she could feel the heat of it and then a moment later Corliss heard the fall of a body whirling around she saw a soldier laying there face down as tendrils of smoke still spiraled from the crater in his skull, Corliss cursed as the call of alarm rose behind her.

“Fire!” Corliss screamed and instantly heard the sounds of more shots as Starish and Borik abandoned the plan of stealth instead opting to strike openly now that they had been discovered.

The Warden whirled around to find another guard not twenty paces from her, his wide eyes still focused on the body behind her.

She expertly drew the pistol from her belt, flipping it end over end, catching the hammer with her thumb and fired into the man’s chest.

The barrel erupted with ethereal blue light that streaked through the soldier, the smoldering hole the only evidence of its assault.

He looked down, his eyes still wide as his mouth made the motion to talk, but no sound came out.

After only a fleeting moment, the man fell to the ground with a meaty thump. Corliss had already turned crouching she quietly made her way around the tent. As she approached the front, Corliss pulled out the second pistol and came face to face with an awesome sight.

Borik stood in the middle of the camp next to the now smoldering fire pit, with a handful of blue resin shells, he pointed the large cannon resting the stock on his upper arm.

Corliss watched the weapon explode as a wash of blue energy took out the three soldiers in front of him. Borik hit the latch at the top of the barrel breaching the chamber and dropping another shell in. With a quick movement of his hand the chamber snapped closed, and he fired into another group of assembling soldiers.

She watched in amazement as Borik did these four more times, the movements practiced and fluid. Any soldier that escaped his blast would be taken out by the streak of energy coming from the treetops. Corliss spied two soldiers using the tents as cover as they tried to flank Borik.

Pointing both pistols she took only a moment to aim gently squeezing of both triggers simultaneously as two blue lines of energy connected with the soldiers, the two dropping, smoking holes in their chest.

Pushing the pistols into their holsters, she unsheathed the ancient sword with one hand and pulled a hatchet with the other.

Corliss was a force of nature as she waded through the last of the soldiers, slashing, blocking and cutting down every last one. Like a deadly dancer, she moved with grace and lethal speed as soldiers dropped before her.

By the time she reached Borik, not a soul stood in the once populated camp. Now nothing but ruin and death stood as a monument to their success.

They searched the camp for any letters or mission statements that might give them a hint as to where these soldiers had been sent. But as with any mission of this type, there was nothing and she didn’t expect to find anything.

The team left the camp, raiding the dead men’s consumables before heading out to make their own camp four miles further down the trail.

Sleep did not come easy for them as the deaths from the camp replayed in there semi sleeping minds.

After a fitful night Corliss awoke before the sun, getting the fire started as she fought to keep the chill from settling into her bones. Sitting as the fire grew, feeding off the dead branches and kindling, Corliss had expertly laid out into the circle of rocks. It was almost hypnotic and helped to keep the demons at bay within her mind, just watching the flames, the blessed silence of her brain in these moments were priceless she reflected. Corliss knew they were close to their destination but the exact location of what had fallen to earth eluded her.

In her mind she reviewed the terrain trying to match the view from the sisters keep to their current location now.

“Morning, Warden,” Came a gentle voice behind her, Corliss didn’t need to turn to know that Starish, was moving out of her tent to join her. She was dressed from head to toe in a heavy, white, fur suit.

It would keep the cold away and help her to blend in with her surroundings should they have another incident like the night before. She came over to the fire, sitting down and pulling out a few pieces of salted jerky, handing one to Corliss they both sat in silence eating the meat for breakfast.

“Do you think we will come across others today?” Starish queried, Corliss shrugging, “I truly hope not, the sisters told us about two groups, there is probably one more out here, but I am not sure we will come across them, and if my memory of the terrain is accurate, we should be close to the landing site” she stated eating the last piece of salted meat and taking a swig from the water skin.

Starish nodded and the two were interrupted by the grunts and moans coming from the tent behind them as Borik woke and moved to get out of his tent.

Corliss and Sharisa exchanged a glance, both smiling as the man moaned and cursed, finally emerging from the cloth tent and lumbering over to sit with the women.

They finished breakfast as they packed up camp, Corliss could see the soldiers keeping a wary eye on the woods around them. As they rode, the first flakes of the day began to fall making visibility limited moving west Corliss found it more difficult to judge there location as the snow grew heavier, looking for any sign of their objective, despite the storm the small group was rewarded when Starish pointed up towards the canopy revealing the myriad of broken branches, like a perfect circle through the canopy, it was hard to miss the tunnel of destruction descending to the ground.

Corliss followed the devastation and Adjusting their direction, the group carefully made their way into the woods, going as far as they could on horseback and then the final hundred feet on foot.

Corliss emerged from the underbrush first, easily finding the location where the line of broken branches ended in an impact.

Approaching, she noticed the indent in the ground and the tracks that circled the area, but there was nothing there, just empty ground and proof that something had been there.

“This isn’t good,” she whispered, coming to the indent in the ground wiping away the snow she found a strange pattern of the tracks. They were footwear but the tread pattern was circular.

Kneeling down, she continued to wipe away the snow around a track and studying it carefully, she had never seen anything like it.

Motioning the team over Starish came to kneel next to her, studying the singular foot tread with an expert eye

“What do you make of this?” Corliss asked looking at the other tracker who seemed lost in thought as she moved her fingers lightly over the ridges emblazoned in the ground.

“I don’t know, it’s a boot pattern, but an odd one” she whispered “Its worn, this isn’t fresh but there are others here as well, someone has been here and left” she said looking up at her.

Corliss nodded “It’s a light tread but a sturdy one, this is a combat shoe but not a typical soldier boot, the person who was here traveled light, this wasn’t our soldiers” she surmised and Starish nodded agreeing with the assessment.

“Track the original one, Borik and I will keep an eye out for the other,” she ordered. Pointing to the large man and with a hand motion ordered him to the perimeter. Guard duty was uneventful, whoever had been out here had left a while ago and there was no sign of anyone else so Corliss and Borik remained on sentry duty as Sharisa followed the tracks.

Corliss took the time to go over the landing site as she knelt down and tried to make sense of the tracks and indentations, allowing them to tell a story as she examined them with an expert eye, something large had come down, from the look of the tracks, both barefoot and then with an odd tread pattern unlike any she had seen, this person had pulled cargo and then left she surmised.

Starish walked over to her with something shiny in her hand Corliss reached out taking the item and running it through her fingers. It made an odd noise but looked like very thin metal with an opening at one end.

“What is this?” she asked, studying the thing Starish shrugged “The opening has some kind of food content so I would think a package of some kind, but like nothing I have ever seen” she responded, moving back to the trail to find more.

Corliss studied it looking the shiny package over carefully, on it was writing that she couldn’t make out and after a moment she slipped it into a leather satchel.

Corliss stood there frustrated Galen had given her very little to go on, much less told her what to expect, she was in over her head and knew it, but that had never stopped her before she thought, there was no way Corliss would return to her father with her head hung low admitting defeat.

They spent the next few days tracking the lone walker, between the two trackers they were able to make out his path. Finally, they emerged on the rocky beach of a river, they could see items strewn at one location. Walking over they found cloth and other items strewn over the rocks, kneeling down Corliss picked up a small metal box, turning it over in her hand, she finally gave up on trying to identify it and pushed it into the leather satchel on her side.

“What the hell happened here” Corliss asked eyeing the alien equipment, she couldn’t even fathom what it was before her.

Sharisa fingered holes in the cloth of what looked like a large pack her blue eyes narrowed as she studied them “Wolves, someone dropped the pack running from wolves” she finally surmised. “Borik, collect that stuff up” Corliss said and received a curt nod from the larger man. Starish walked up and down the bank eyeing the other side as she did. “Chances are we have lost his trail; I am not confident we can pick it back up,” she said.

Corliss looked over the detritus as Borik continued to police the beach. She looked over the tread marks recognizing them from around the crash site. Someone, not something had come down and crashed she thought looking out over the Woodline across the river.

“Okay, you two are going back to the keep, I am going to continue to track this person or people, report to Galen that I am still on the trail” she finished and turned to look at the two of them. She could see both wanted to protest but Corliss was in charge and she had given an order. With an irritated nod they both headed back to their horses as Corliss continued to walk up and down the beach.

Corliss knew the stories of the first men, how they had descended in metal tears from the sky and the power they wielded, could this be like that, the Mother Superior had called it a metal tear, if this was in fact a fallen one, then this person would have the power of the ancients she shivered at the thought and then her mind considered the number of people looking for him, if this person indeed did possess the powers talked about in the old stories, he could change the balance of power in the territory forever.

She shivered at the thought of what such a man would be like.
